claim: BIND_PG-1.md §B-3 frames the audit question as reconciling CAPABILITY_MANIFEST.json (entry_count 113) against the live MCP tool surface (~200 observed), implying the two are the same kind of registry at different points of drift.
reality: CAPABILITY_MANIFEST.json is a governance-artifact catalog (canonical_id, path, version, status, layer L0-L6, expose_to_chat, representations, interface_version, fingerprint) generated by platform/src/scripts/manifest/build.ts — it catalogs documentation/data assets (e.g. first entry is CGP_AUDIT_v1_0.md, a markdown file), not MCP tool registrations. It has zero fields describing an MCP tool (no input_schema, no archetype, no tool_role). The actual MCP-tool-facing registry lives at platform/src/lib/retrieval/registry/ (CapabilityDescriptor type in types.ts, 119 distinct marsys://tool/* URIs found across platform/src/lib/retrieval/registry/layers/**). Comparing 113 (doc-artifact manifest) against the live MCP tool count is a category error — they are disjoint systems serving disjoint purposes.

evidence.quote: Lane R-1 re-derives the exact live count mechanically ... and reconciles against CAPABILITY_MANIFEST.json (entry_count: 113, entries: 113 ...) ... likely undercounts the served surface

recommended_action: Retire the 113-vs-200 framing entirely. The document that should be reconciled against the live MCP surface is platform/src/lib/retrieval/registry/ (the CapabilityDescriptor registry), not CAPABILITY_MANIFEST.json. Any future PARIPRASHNA_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE §8 discussion of 'one registry' should name platform/src/lib/retrieval/registry/ explicitly and stop citing CAPABILITY_MANIFEST.json's entry_count as an MCP-capability figure.

claim: platform-mcp/src/server.ts's own census comment (lines 460-522) computes REGISTERED_TOOL_COUNT = 120 via an itemized per-file breakdown, presented as the authoritative recount ("BA-P1 recount 2026-07-03 — authoritative", later incremented for D-2 lanes).
reality: The itemized breakdown undercounts four of its own cited files. Actual server.tool()/registerTool() call counts in the source: registry_bridge.ts = 25 (census says 20, +5: chart_snapshot, get_graha_yuddha, judgment_query, graha_portrait, pact_query are registered but not itemized); register_p1_synthesis.ts = 6 (census says 3, +3: prashna_undertaking_get, synth_chart_brief_get, synth_tail_divergence_get missing from the comment); register_p1_aliases.ts = 55 total (35 direct server.tool() calls + 20 via regAlias()/globalAlias() helper calls including ganita_ayurdaya_get, ganita_medical_get, ganita_vastu_get, ganita_vichara_get, ganita_sensitive_degrees_get, ganita_yoga_firings_get, kala_priority_ranking_get, ref_sign_medical_get, resolve_entity — census says 45, +10); register_p2_dasha_lord.ts registers 1 tool (ganita_dasha_lord_capability_get) that is imported and called in server.ts (line 364) but never appears anywhere in the running-total arithmetic (+1 uncounted). Sum of corrections: 120 + 5 + 3 + 10 + 1 = 139, which exactly matches the live tool count observed in this session's connected mcp__marsys-jis-direct__* tool listing.

evidence.quote: // Tool count computed from registration calls (BA-P1 recount 2026-07-03 — authoritative):

recommended_action: Fix the census comment/REGISTERED_TOOL_COUNT to 139 (or compute it programmatically from server.registrationCount at runtime instead of a hand-maintained comment — this is the same drift class GA.1/B.8 warns about). Add register_p2_dasha_lord.ts to the itemization. This directly informs A-02 (alias deletion) and A-03 (registry projections) sizing in the target architecture — any headcount used to plan the MCP-compact ~25-35 umbrella count should be derived from the corrected 139, and specifically account for the fact that most of the excess over the platform registry's 119 URIs is Phase-1 naming aliases (many-to-one onto the same underlying capability).

claim: Baseline fact for reconciliation: the platform-side capability registry (platform/src/lib/retrieval/registry/, CapabilityDescriptor-typed) is a separate, smaller set of distinct capabilities than the MCP tool-name surface, because MCP tool names alias onto the same registry URI.
reality: grep across platform/src/lib/retrieval/registry/layers/**/*.ts for the marsys://tool/ URI pattern yields 119 distinct URIs across 104 files. This is the 'one registry' D-08/A-08 in §1 refers to. Live MCP tool-name count is 139 (see PG1-R1-0002); CAPABILITY_MANIFEST.json's 113 is an unrelated doc-artifact catalog (see PG1-R1-0001). None of the three numbers (113, 119, 139) should be treated as interchangeable measures of 'the registry'.
recommended_action: Adopt 119 (platform registry URI count) as the authoritative 'one registry' baseline figure in any future revision of §8.3-8.4; state explicitly that the MCP surface (139 tool names) is a many-to-one alias layer over it.

reality: None of the three projections exist in the current tree. `marsys_drill` appears only inside architecture/brief markdown files (PARIPRASHNA_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE_v0_1.md, RETRIEVAL_PLAN_INDUSTRY_CONSULT_v1_0.md, RETRIEVAL_PLANE_ELEVATION_PLAN_v1_0.md, MCP_CHANNEL_WORKSTREAM_HANDOFF_v1_0.md), never in platform/src or platform-mcp/src source. This is consistent with the document's own framing (target-state, A-03 is a 'proposed' design conclusion, not a current-state claim) — marking unverifiable-as-target rather than stale, since the doc does not assert this is already built.

evidence.quote: `marsys_drill` | The single dispatcher tool in the MCP-compact projection that fans out to leaf capabilities via drill pointers. | Proposed, A-03 |

claim: n/a — descriptor completeness check requested by the lane charge.
reality: Registration-path sampling across the four largest MCP tool-registration files shows a mixed and only partially registry-backed surface: register_p1_aliases.ts routes 17 of its ~55 registrations through callPlatformPrimitive (registry-backed); register_p1_synthesis.ts routes 13 of its 6 tool registrations' underlying calls through callPlatformPrimitive (multiple calls per tool); registry_bridge.ts routes only 3 of its 25 tool registrations through callPlatformPrimitive directly (others likely use platformQuery or other DB-facing helpers not grepped here); register_p1_ganita.ts's 9 tools use neither callPlatformPrimitive nor platformQuery/db.query/pool.query in a simple grep, i.e. their calling mechanism is unidentified from this pass and needs a closer read. This means 'registration path per tool' (registry-backed / sidecar / alias / direct) cannot be fully machine-derived from a single grep pattern — a proper census needs to trace each tool's handler body, not just import statements.
recommended_action: A full registration-path census requires a dedicated script that resolves each server.tool() handler body to its terminal call (callPlatformPrimitive vs platformQuery vs sidecar fetch vs regAlias-wrapped delegate), not a follow-up grep pass. Recording as a scoped defect in audit methodology rather than a claim about the architecture doc.
